Synthetic release-review exercise. Use only the supplied evidence. State one concrete finding and one next check in at most two sentences. Do not invent measurements or claim a deployment happened. The source review, test review and rollout review are separate tasks.

SOURCE_REVIEW_MATERIAL
A fictional checkout service introduces an idempotency key for POST /orders. The key is unique per customer and stored with a request-body hash and order id. On a duplicate key, the service returns the existing order only when the body hash matches; a changed body receives HTTP 409. Database writes and key registration share a transaction. The old handler retried the payment call before recording the order, which could charge twice after a timeout. The new handler forwards the same key to the payment provider. The migration creates a unique index on customer_id plus idempotency_key; the index is built online.

TEST_REVIEW_MATERIAL
Synthetic test report for the checkout change: same key and same payload returns the same order; same key and different payload returns HTTP 409; two concurrent requests with the same key create one row. Simulated payment timeouts are retried with the original provider key. A database rollback test confirms no key remains registered when order creation aborts. A process termination between provider response and database commit has not yet been tested. Load tests were not run, so the report has no throughput or P99 claim.

ROLLOUT_REVIEW_MATERIAL
Synthetic rollout proposal: create the index before enabling the handler; enable it for an internal customer cohort, then five percent of traffic. Watch duplicate payment alerts, HTTP 409 rates, database lock waits and payment-provider timeouts. Keep the old handler behind a feature flag. Rollback disables new traffic to the handler but retains idempotency records so already submitted requests remain deduplicated. An operator must verify the provider's key-retention window before widening the cohort. There is currently no scheduled production deployment and no observed rollout result.
Review the source material. Give a finding and next check.
